item.title: Goose database migration tool supports Go functions and out-of-order changes
item.description:
Goose database migration tool supports Go functions and out-of-order changes

Goose is a database migration tool available as both a CLI and a library. It allows developers to manage database schemas by creating incremental SQL changes or Go functions.

🔍 Overview

The tool supports migrations for multiple database systems. It works against Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, Spanner, SQLite, YDB, ClickHouse, MSSQL, and Vertica.

🧩 How it works

Goose supports specific migration formats and operational features:

  • Go migrations written as plain functions.
  • Embedded migrations.
  • Out-of-order migrations.
  • Seeding data.
  • Environment variable substitution in SQL migrations.

⚙️ Key details

The CLI includes flags for configuring migration behavior. The following table details specific flags and their functions:

Flag Description
-allow-missing Applies missing (out-of-order) migrations
-certfile File path to root CA’s certificates in pem format (only supported on MySQL)
-dir Directory with migration files (default “.”, can be set via GOOSE_MIGRATION_DIR)
-env Load environment variables from file (default .env)
-no-color Disable color output (NO_COLOR env variable supported)
-no-versioning Apply migration commands with no versioning, in file order
-s Use sequential numbering for new migrations
-ssl-cert File path to SSL certificates in pem format (only supported on MySQL)
-ssl-key File path to SSL key in pem format (only supported on MySQL)
-table Migrations table name (default “goose_db_version”)
-timeout Maximum allowed duration for queries to run

🚀 Availability

Goose is available via several installation methods:

  • Go Install: go install github.com/pressly/goose/v3/cmd/goose@latest installs the binary to your $GOPATH/bin directory.
  • Homebrew: Available for macOS users.
  • Docker: A container image is available for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.
    • The container image has no shell and supports .sql migrations only.
    • The working directory is /migrations.
    • Tags include vX.Y.Z, vX.Y, vX, and latest.
    • Dockerfiles can copy the binary using: COPY --from=ghcr.io/pressly/goose:v3.30.1 /usr/local/bin/goose /usr/local/bin/goose

#Goose #Database #Go #CLI #Migrations

Source: pressly/goose

item.title: Langfuse CLI v4 released with new commands and API versioning
item.description:
Langfuse CLI v4 released with new commands and API versioning

Langfuse has released a new CLI tool, @langfuse/cli, which allows users to interact with the Langfuse API directly from the command line. This new release includes updates to command aliases, input handling for complex JSON structures, and specific versioning rules for self-hosted versus cloud deployments.

📦 Package details

  • Package name: @langfuse/cli
  • Executable: langfuse
  • Legacy name: Previously published under langfuse-cli; the new name is recommended for all future use.

⚙️ Configuration and Host Selection

The CLI does not automatically read .env files. Users must manually configure API access and host selection. Host selection follows a specific priority order:

Priority Configuration Method
1 LANGFUSE_BASE_URL
2 LANGFUSE_HOST
3 EU default

To authenticate, users create a project API key pair under Project settings → API Keys.

🧩 Command and Input Features

  • Lossless input: --body-json and --body-file flags provide a lossless input path for nested objects, arrays, unions, and free-form JSON.
  • Pagination: The CLI can fetch every page of a paginated list, supporting both page- and cursor-based endpoints, with a maximum of 1000 items.
  • Aliases: OpenAPI tags and explicit route versions remain accepted aliases (e.g., scores-v3 list for the canonical scores list).
  • Schema: Verbose OpenAPI operationId values are available in api schema --json but are never required as CLI commands.

🌐 Availability and Versioning

  • V3 API Snapshots: Available on self-hosted deployments only.
  • Langfuse Cloud: Supports v4 and up.
  • Backward Compatibility: Users can use an API snapshot compatible with an older self-hosted deployment.

#Langfuse #CLI #API #DeveloperTools

Source: langfuse/langfuse-cli

item.title: DSPyGen Offers a Rails-Inspired CLI for Building DSPy Modules
item.description:
DSPyGen Offers a Rails-Inspired CLI for Building DSPy Modules

DSPyGen is a command-line framework for developing language-model pipelines with DSPy, using a structured, modular approach inspired by Ruby on Rails.

🔍 Overview

DSPyGen is described as a framework for the DSPy project, which works with language models such as GPT, BERT, and Llama. Its stated aim is to simplify creating, developing, and deploying LM pipelines. The project says it was influenced by the work of Sean Chatman and James I. Chatman.

🧩 How it works

The CLI provides commands to initialize a project, generate DSPy modules, run a module, and serve a REST API:

1
2
3
4
5
6
7

dspygen init my_project
cd my_project

dspygen module new -cn TextSummarizer -i "text" -o "summary"
dspygen module text_summarizer call "Gettysburg address"

docker-compose up app

The dspygen module new command creates modules. Its listed options are:

  • --class-name, -cn: required module class name.
  • --inputs, -i: comma-separated input names.
  • --output, -o: output name.
  • --help: show command help and exit.

⚙️ Example modules

Example Inputs Output
Text summarization text summary
Sentiment analysis text sentiment
YouTube comment generation vid_title,words viral_comment
Machine translation source_text,target_language translated_text
Code generation prompt generated_code

The project also says it generates a mocked pytest module for provided Python source code.

🚀 Model setup examples

The examples show initializing DSPy with OpenAI and Groq, and initializing Ollama with init_ol:

  • OpenAI: init_dspy(model="gpt-4o", max_tokens=500)
  • Groq: The instructions say to obtain an API key from Groq and modify .env as demonstrated in .envDemo; the example uses init_dspy(model="llama3-70b-8192", lm_class=Groq, max_tokens=8000).
  • Ollama: The instructions say to install Ollama, then show init_ol(model="llama3", max_tokens=2000) followed by a call to the text summarizer module.

#DSPy #AIdevelopment #LanguageModels #Python #CLI

Source: seanchatmangpt/dspygen

item.title: Gemini Notebook CLI adds programmatic access and encrypted login storage
item.description:
Gemini Notebook CLI adds programmatic access and encrypted login storage

Gemini Notebook now offers programmatic access via a command-line interface (CLI), Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, and AI agent skills. This update also introduces an option to encrypt Google login credentials in a computer’s keychain.

🧩 How it works

Programmatic access to Gemini Notebook is available through three methods:

  • Command-line interface (CLI)
  • Model Context Protocol (MCP) server
  • AI agent skills

Users can connect tools in three commands:

  1. Install (provides nlm and the MCP server): uv tool install notebooklm-mcp-cli
  2. Sign in to Google account: nlm login
  3. Connect AI tools: nlm setup

🔐 Security details

Saved Google logins can now be encrypted with the key kept in the computer’s keychain instead of a plain file. This feature is optional and changes nothing unless explicitly enabled.

  • Recommended for personal computers: nlm auth storage set protected
  • Alternative: Use the nlm setup wizard and select the ‘Credentials Protection’ option.
  • Servers, cron, Docker, and SSH setups can keep the plain file.
  • Personal and consumer accounts are tested regularly.

⚙️ Enterprise support

Gemini Notebook Enterprise support is currently experimental. The documented notebook.cloud.google.com host has been live-verified with a project-qualified global deployment. Other Enterprise host variants may require additional validation.

🎬 Demo resources

The developer notes the tool is free and built in spare time, with a coffee helping cover the real time and resources required for testing every Gemini Notebook feature. A collection of videos demonstrates various aspects of the workflow:

item.title: Nucleoid adds terminal workspace, bare-word syntax, and comment updates
item.description:
Nucleoid adds terminal workspace, bare-word syntax, and comment updates

Nucleoid has updated its developer experience and language syntax with a new full-screen terminal workspace, support for bare-word assignments, and changes to how comments and conditional logic are handled.

🔍 Overview

Nucleoid is a next-generation logic programming language built on structured objects and their relationships, extending the traditional Knowledge Graph. It uses a minimum-token syntax for logic representation and a declarative execution model, eliminating the need for LLMs to manually manage control flow, state propagation, and other imperative constructs.

🧩 How it works

The new interactive interface offers a top-level tab layout, with two tabs reserved for future views. A multiline editor sits at the bottom, featuring autocomplete for keywords, built-ins, and model properties, plus in-session input and result history. Results can be inspected in Text, JSON, or Table formats without re-running the program; arrays of objects render as table rows, while other JSON values display in property/value or index/value views.

Key input behaviors include:

  • Enter inserts a newline.
  • F5 runs the entire editor content.
  • Ctrl-J inserts an automatically indented newline.
  • Tab accepts autocomplete or indents.
  • Ctrl-Space opens suggestions.
  • Ctrl-P / Ctrl-N recalls input while preserving an unfinished draft.
  • F1-F3 switch tabs, F6 changes the result view, and Ctrl-Up / Ctrl-Down select earlier results.
  • Mouse clicks select tabs, views, and results; click/drag edits the cursor/selection, and the wheel scrolls individual panes.
  • Ctrl-C cancels input, Ctrl-Q exits, and .help lists all controls.

⚙️ Key details

  • Assignment Syntax: Assignments can be written as target is value. Quotes are optional around a single word. For example, a is 5 and o.x is "good" are valid. If the value is a bare word that does not match a defined variable, class, function, or built-in, it stores its own text.
  • Conditional Branches: In conditionals like a is A if c else B, a bare word in a branch is read as a variable, class, function, or built-in if it exists; otherwise, it reads as its own text. Parenthesized operands are not treated as words, so a is (A if c else B) requires A and B to be defined.
  • List and Dictionary Items: Inside is values, list items, dictionary values, or named arguments can also be bare words.
  • Comments: Hash (#), double-slash (//), and non-nesting block comments (/* ... */) all work in files and interactive interfaces. Comments take delimiter priority outside literals, meaning // is a comment, not an empty regex (use /(?:)/ for an empty-matching regex). Comments retain newlines and source positions and cannot join tokens or supply indentation. Unclosed block comments report SyntaxError: Unterminated block comment at its opening slash.
  • Plain Mode: Running nucleoid --plain provides a line-oriented interface. Piped stdin or redirected stdout automatically selects this mode. Body lines are prefilled with indentation after the .. prompt, and blank lines submit the block.

🚀 Availability

Install the CLI from crates.io using the command: cargo install nucleoid. The standard nucleoid command opens the full-screen terminal workspace from any directory. File execution and the --json and --graph flags retain their existing behavior. References NUC 76, NUC 93, and NUC 94 document the removal of the --c-style-comments, --is-assignment, and --conditional-words flags, respectively.

#Nucleoid #LogicProgramming #CLI #KnowledgeGraph #Rust

Source: NucleoidAI/Nucleoid

item.title: OpenScreen: Free, Open-Source Screen Recording App with AI Editing
item.description:
OpenScreen: Free, Open-Source Screen Recording App with AI Editing

OpenScreen is a new open-source desktop application that turns raw screen recordings into polished demos without watermarks or subscriptions. It supports Windows, macOS, and Linux, offering features like AI-powered editing, automatic captions, and GPU-accelerated export.

📸 What It Does

OpenScreen is designed to help users record their screen and instantly transform the result into share-ready content for platforms like YouTube, X, Reddit, or documentation sites.

Key capabilities include:

  • Record a specific window or your entire screen
  • Capture both microphone and system audio
  • Webcam overlay with picture-in-picture mode
  • Auto and manual zooms with adjustable settings
  • Custom cursor size, smoothing, and click effects
  • Automatic on-device captions with offline transcription
  • An AI editing assistant that applies changes from natural language descriptions
  • Support for multiple background options including wallpapers and gradients
  • Motion blur and per-segment speed control on the timeline
  • Text, arrow, and image annotations with animation presets
  • Timeline snapping guides and audio waveform visualization
  • Export to MP4 or GIF with GPU-accelerated rendering (Metal, D3D11, Vulkan)

⚙️ Key Details

Feature Description
Licensing MIT License, 100% free for personal and commercial use
Platforms Windows, macOS, Linux
AI Assistant Works with Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Mistral, OpenRouter, MiniMax, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
CLI Support Headless recording, JSON editing, and rendering via command line
Caption Languages Arabic, Czech, English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Turkish, Vietnamese, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese

Development started with Siddharth Vaddem, who archived the original repository after v1.5.0 before moving development to a new repository under the same name and MIT license. The project remains actively maintained, though users should expect rough edges and occasional breaking changes to the project format and CLI.

#OpenSource #ScreenRecording #AIEditing #GPUAcceleration #CLI

Source: getopenscreen/openscreen

item.title: CLI tool adds automated scoring and checklist for Agent projects
item.description:
CLI tool adds automated scoring and checklist for Agent projects

The agent-handbook project released a new CLI tool that can automatically score an Agent codebase against a five‑pillar checklist drawn from its 31‑chapter Chinese handbook.

🔍 Overview

  • Provides a static scan of your Agent project and reports which of the five pillars are missing.
  • Maps gaps to the exact chapter and section of the handbook that explains the concept.
  • Generates a 0–10 score with concrete remediation suggestions.

🛠️ How it works

  • The command handbook doctor . walks the code, checks it against the five‑pillar criteria, and produces a Markdown table of results.
  • --md flag outputs the table so it can be pasted directly into an issue, README, or PR comment; the tool also posts the report automatically to the PR and the Job Summary.
  • handbook search <keyword> performs full‑text search across all 31 chapters, returning chapter, line number, and snippet.
  • handbook new <name> scaffolds a new Agent project that already satisfies all five pillars, earning a full score.
  • The tool runs with zero dependencies, using only the Python standard library, and works offline because the handbook data is bundled with the package.

⚙️ Key details

Command Description
handbook doctor . Five‑pillar health check, 0–10 score + remediation suggestions
handbook doctor . --md Output Markdown table for easy inclusion in issues/README
handbook search 上下文压缩 Full‑text search of the 31‑chapter handbook, returns chapter, line, snippet
handbook new my-agent Generate an Agent skeleton that scores full on the five pillars
Chapter Title Quick note
00 新手快速入门 10 分钟跑通第一个 Agent
03 LangGraph 图编排 复杂工作流、状态机、检查点
04 CrewAI 多智能体 角色化团队、任务分配
06 LlamaIndex RAG 文档检索、向量数据库
07 Dify 低代码 可视化拖拽构建应用
11 MCP 协议 标准化工具连接（含 2026 无状态核心）
14 记忆系统与状态管理 Mem0、向量记忆、持久化
16 调试与可观测性 LangSmith、日志、追踪
19 Agent 通用工具箱 工具注册中心 / 审批网关 / 成本追踪等六件套
20 Codex CLI MCP 集成、四种审批模式、沙箱隔离
21 DeepSeek Harness 四种模式、SWE‑bench、500+ 插件
23 Aider 代码助手 多模型、Git 集成、会话恢复
25 Harness Engineering 五支柱：2026 年 Agent 上生产的分水岭
30 Agent 评测体系 EDD、三层评测金字塔
99 中英对照术语表 130+ 术语通俗解释

🚀 Availability

  • Install with zero‑install uvx: uvx agent-handbook doctor .
  • Alternative: pipx run agent-handbook doctor .
  • Or install via pip: pip install agent-handbook
  • The handbook chapters are packaged together, so the tool works fully offline.

💡 Why it matters

  • Turns the handbook’s methodology into a concrete, checkable checklist for developers.
  • Provides immediate, actionable feedback directly in the code review workflow.
  • Low barrier to entry: no external dependencies, works offline, and integrates with common CI/PR systems.
  • Supports rapid prototyping (handbook new) and ongoing quality monitoring (handbook doctor).

#AIAgents #CLI #AgentHandbook #DevTools

Source: Xwh630/ai-agent-handbook

item.title: AI‑Powered CLI Pipeline Generates Custom PDFs for Job Applications
item.description:
AI‑Powered CLI Pipeline Generates Custom PDFs for Job Applications

Um conjunto de agentes de IA (CrewAI + AWS Bedrock/Claude) lê a descrição de uma vaga e a base profissional da pessoa e gera currículos personalizados em PDF/LaTeX, em PT ou EN, sem inventar informações e preservando toda a trajetória de carreira. O autor, profissional de TI com mais de 30 anos de carreira, usou o método e foi contratado 5 meses depois.

🔍 Overview

  • Ferramenta: CLI com agentes de IA que automatiza a parte mais trabalhosa do método, produzindo currículos sob medida para cada vaga.
  • Método: passo a passo que organiza a busca, da construção do perfil às retrospectivas que refinam o processo.
  • Abordagem: tratado como um pipeline de dados, em que cada etapa recebe a saída da anterior.

🧩 How it Works

  • Cria‑se um arquivo profile_truth.md contendo a versão longa e honesta da carreira.
  • Todo currículo e toda resposta de entrevista são gerados a partir desse arquivo.
  • A IA propõe reordenação, resumo e tradução; o usuário decide o que usar.
  • A IA não pode inventar informações; nada sai com o seu nome sem você ler.
  • Uma planilha simples rastreia quais currículos e fontes de vagas geram respostas.
  • Ao fim de cada prazo definido, uma retrospectiva transforma os dados coletados em ajustes no processo.
  • Duas trilhas seguem o mesmo método; a diferença está em quem produz o currículo (prompts em chat de IA vs. CLI que gera os arquivos).

⚙️ Key Details

  • Requisitos de ambiente
    • Assistente de IA
    • Python 3.9+ (ou Python 3.12)
    • LaTeX para gerar PDFs
    • Chave de API de um provedor de IA
  • Segurança
    • Diretórios input/, data/, outputs/ e privado/ estão no .gitignore.
    • Chaves de API ficam somente no .env, que também é ignorado pelo git.
    • Senhas, documentos e dados bancários nunca entram em prompts.
  • Limitações da CLI
    • Cobre apenas parte do método; não busca nem tria vagas.
    • Usa prompts prontos em um chat de IA para gerar o conteúdo.
  • Funções automáticas
    • Revisão de cobertura automática por posição; prompt disponível para identificar lacunas da vaga.
    • Preparação de entrevista com rascunho automático.
  • Avisos
    • A IA pode errar datas, exagerar resultados e trocar números.
    • O projeto não serve para fabricar experiência, burlar triagem ou candidatar‑se em massa sem ler as vagas.
  • Documentação
    • Tutorial completo em meu-emprego-novo-pipeline/README.md.

🚀 Availability

  • O código está organizado em pastas (input/, data/, outputs/, privado/) protegidas por .gitignore.
  • O usuário executa um comando que dispara os agentes e gera os arquivos de currículo.
  • As duas trilhas (uso de prompts vs. CLI) utilizam o mesmo perfil‑mestre escrito em profile_truth.md.

💡 Why it Matters

  • Gera currículos personalizados sem inventar informações, preservando a integridade da carreira.
  • Automatiza a parte mais trabalhosa da preparação de candidatura, permitindo foco na revisão e no ajuste contínuo.
  • Fornece métricas simples (planilha) para avaliar quais abordagens geram respostas, apoiando decisões baseadas em dados.

#AIAgents #ResumeAutomation #CLI #CareerTech

Source: R238Company/meu-emprego-novo

item.title: Open‑Source RemoveMacAI Tool Deletes Apple Intelligence Models, Frees Up Storage
item.description:
Open‑Source RemoveMacAI Tool Deletes Apple Intelligence Models, Frees Up Storage

A new open‑source command‑line utility called RemoveMacAI lets macOS users delete Apple Intelligence models and disable its bundled AI features in a single step, reclaiming roughly a dozen gigabytes of disk space.

🔧 What RemoveMacAI Does

  • ‘RemoveMacAI’ switches off Apple’s AI features, deletes its AI models, and blocks them from being downloaded again.
  • It removes the on‑disk foundation models, which the developer says take up about 12 GB of space (some users report even more).
  • The changes persist across macOS updates.
  • Dictation continues to work after removal.
  • The tool provides a removemacai revert command to re‑enable all features and allow the models to download again.
  • A removemacai status command shows the size of each individual AI model on the Mac.

“I wrote RemoveMacAI to do all of it in one go.”

📦 Storage Impact

  • Apple Intelligence models remain on disk by default, occupying about 12 GB according to the developer.
  • A user measured 35.05 GB of space labeled “Apple Intelligence” on a MacBook Air.
  • Running RemoveMacAI deletes these models, freeing the corresponding storage.

⚙️ How It Works

  1. The tool toggles off the following AI‑related features:
    • Siri
    • Writing Tools
    • Genmoji
    • Image Playground
    • The ChatGPT extension
    • All summary functions
  2. It then deletes the stored foundation models from the file system.
  3. Finally, it prevents macOS from re‑downloading the models unless the user runs removemacai revert.

📋 Feature List

Feature Action performed by RemoveMacAI
Siri Turned off
Writing Tools Turned off
Genmoji Turned off
Image Playground Turned off
ChatGPT extension Turned off
Summaries Turned off

📆 Availability

  • The utility is open‑source and was announced by its developer on Reddit.
  • It replaces the single Settings toggle that existed for disabling Apple Intelligence before it was removed in macOS 27, where the models stayed on disk and settings were split across multiple panes (including several under Screen Time).

💡 Why It Matters

  • Users who prefer not to run Apple’s on‑device AI can now remove the models entirely, reclaiming storage without losing core functionality like Dictation.
  • The tool simplifies what previously required navigating about a dozen settings across various preference panes.
  • By blocking future downloads, it ensures the storage savings remain until the user decides to restore the features.

#AppleIntelligence #macOS #OpenSource #CLI

Source: An open-source tool lets you delete 12GB of Apple Intelligence data on macOS

item.title: OpenHands CLI Launches Lightweight Binary for Local AI Agent Development
item.description:
OpenHands CLI Launches Lightweight Binary for Local AI Agent Development

A new lightweight OpenHands CLI is available as a standalone binary executable. Powered by the OpenHands Software Agent SDK, it lets you run an OpenHands agent directly in your terminal, favorite IDE, CI pipelines, local browser, or secure OpenHands Cloud sandboxes. The project is no longer actively maintained, and users are advised to consider Agent Canvas for a fully open‑source, customizable, local AI coding agent experience.

🔍 Overview

  • Provides a binary‑based command‑line interface for OpenHands agents.
  • Supports multiple execution environments: terminal (TUI), IDEs, headless scripts, web UI, and full GUI server.
  • Distributed under the MIT License.

🛠️ How it Works

  • Requirements: Python 3.12+ and uv 0.11.6 or newer.
  • Installation:
    • Binary: curl -fsSL https://install.openhands.dev/install.sh | sh
    • Via uv: uv tool install openhands --python 3.12
  • First‑run setup guides you through LLM configuration.
  • Configuration files are stored under ~/.openhands/:
    • agent_settings.json – persisted agent settings.
    • cli_config.json – CLI/TUI preferences.
    • mcp.json – Model Context Protocol server configuration.
  • Environment variables such as LLM_API_KEY, LLM_MODEL, and LLM_BASE_URL are ignored by default; use --override-with-envs to apply them (not persisted).

⚙️ Features

  • Interactive terminal UI (openhands).
  • IDE integration (openhands acp) for Toad, Zed, VSCode, JetBrains, etc.
  • Headless mode (openhands --headless -t "task") for CI, scripts, and automation.
  • Browser‑based TUI (openhands web).
  • Full web GUI server (openhands serve).
  • Extensible via Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
  • Action confirmation by default; auto‑approve with --always-approve or --yolo.
  • LLM‑based security analysis with --llm-approve.
  • Resume recent conversations with openhands --resume.

📋 Commands

Command Description
openhands Launch interactive terminal UI
openhands --headless -t "task" Run in headless mode for CI/CD, scripts, automation
openhands web Open browser‑based TUI
openhands serve Start full web GUI server
openhands --always-approve (or --yolo) Auto‑approve all actions
openhands --llm-approve Use LLM‑based security analyzer
openhands --resume List recent conversations

📦 Availability

  • Binary install script and uv package are provided.
  • Requires Python 3.12+ and uv 0.11.6+.
  • Project is no longer actively maintained; users are encouraged to explore Agent Canvas for an open‑source, customizable alternative.

💡 Why it matters

  • Enables developers to run AI‑powered coding agents locally across a wide range of environments without needing a cloud service.
  • Offers both interactive and automation‑focused modes, facilitating integration into development workflows and CI pipelines.
  • Open source licensing (MIT) allows unrestricted use and modification.

#OpenHands #AIagents #CLI #Automation

Source: OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI

item.title: Agent Reach provides free open-source internet capabilities for CLI agents
item.description:
Agent Reach provides free open-source internet capabilities for CLI agents

Agent Reach has been introduced as an open-source tool that enables CLI-based agents to access and extract data from various websites and platforms without API fees.

⚙️ Key details

  • License: MIT License
  • Requirement: Python 3.10+
  • Security: Cookies are stored locally and are not uploaded or transmitted.
  • Compatibility: Works with any agent that can run command-line interface (CLI) instructions, including Claude Code, OpenClaw, Cursor, and Windsurf.
  • Diagnostics: Includes agent-reach doctor to check connectivity and provide repair instructions.

🧩 How it works

Agent Reach integrates with other tools and platforms to provide data extraction and connectivity:

  • BrowserAct: Supports extracting arbitrary data from complex sites such as Amazon, LinkedIn, and Google Maps.
  • CoreClaw: Provides over 100 ready-made data collection tools for platforms including TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube.
  • Astraflow: Supports one-click calling of 200+ models, including Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4/V3, Qwen 3, GLM5.2, and happyhorse.
  • OpenClaw: Can be deployed on Tencent Cloud Lighthouse to integrate Agent Reach via conversation.

item.title: Claude Code 2.1.269 Release Adds Plugin Evals and Enhanced Workflow Controls
item.description:
Claude Code 2.1.269 Release Adds Plugin Evals and Enhanced Workflow Controls

Claude Code has released version 2.1.269, a broad update introducing plugin evaluation tools, output-style switching, and expanded telemetry and workflow controls across CLI, VS Code, web, and Slack experiences.

⚙️ Key Details

New Features

  • Claude Plugin Eval: A tool to run a plugin’s eval suite against Claude Code to receive scored, reproducible results in JSON and HTML report formats.
  • Output-Style Switching: The /output-style [name] command allows users to list and switch output styles, including within cloud, headless sessions, and via Remote Control.
  • Workflow and Telemetry Enhancements:
    • Added CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS (range 1–256) to increase the concurrent agent limit for inference-bound fan-outs in the Workflow tool.
    • Added OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_REPOSITORY to tag OpenTelemetry metrics and events with vcs.* repository attributes.
    • Added CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS to extend the LLM gateway discovery timeout (default 3s).
  • UI and Tooling Updates:
    • A new spinner tip suggests using /focus for a view featuring only the prompt, a one-line work summary, and the response.
    • Bash tool results now include a diff of files changed when bashEditDiffEnabled is set.

Fixed Issues

Area Fix Description
Prompt Cache Fixed partial invalidation after responses were cut off at output-token limits and fixed context re-sending issues after interruptions.
Terminal Resolved issues with F1/F2/F4 in kitty-protocol, Delete in st, Alt+arrows in rxvt-unicode, and Shift+punctuation in WezTerm.
Plugins Fixed synced MCP servers not connecting on remote session resume and ensured LSP servers (e.g., rust-analyzer) receive an exit signal even if shutdown fails.
Sessions Fixed headless sessions losing replies during model switches or retries, and resolved reports of “waiting for your input” while background agents were active.
General Fixed CMYK JPEG decoding failures and restored prompt suggestions for languages without spaces (e.g., Japanese, Chinese, Thai).

#ClaudeCode #AI #DeveloperTools #CLI

item.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude Code Agentic CLI and Model Updates
item.description:
Anthropic Introduces Claude Code Agentic CLI and Model Updates

Claude Code is a new agentic CLI designed to read codebases, execute commands, and modify files using a layered system of permissions, hooks, MCP integrations, and subagents.

🧩 How it works

Claude Code utilizes various agents and permission modes to manage development tasks:

  • Subagents: These can run in the background by default. They are supported up to a default depth of 3 (configurable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=1 to disable) with a maximum of 20 concurrent subagents (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS).
  • Permission Modes: The default permission mode is “Manual” across the CLI, VS Code, and JetBrains. However, “Auto” mode will be the default for new Pro, Max, and Team sessions starting August 14, 2026.
  • Background Capabilities: Background agents can commit, push, and open draft PRs upon completing code in a worktree. They utilize the Notification hook (agent_needs_input/agent_completed).

⚙️ Key details

Recent version updates have introduced the following technical changes:

Version Update/Feature
v2.1.198 Subagents run in background by default; Claude in Chrome reaches general availability.
v2.1.199 Supports up to 5 stacked slash-skill invocations; automatic retry for transient 429 errors for subscribers.
v2.1.202 Adds “Dynamic workflow size” control in /config and separates /review from /code-review.
v2.1.203–205 /doctor becomes a full diagnostic and correction review (alias /checkup).
v2.1.217 Subagents stop generating their own subagents by default.
v2.1.218 /code-review and skills with context: fork move to background subagents; /deep-research requires explicit invocation.
v2.1.219 Re-enables nested subagents up to depth 3; adds DirectoryAdded hook and sandbox.network.strictAllowlist.

🚀 Availability

Model availability and pricing vary by license and plan:

  • Claude Opus 5: Default for Max, Team Premium, Enterprise (from v2.1.251), and Anthropic API. It features a 1M context window, 128K maximum output, reasoning enabled by default, “high” default effort, and a knowledge cutoff of May 2026. Pricing is $5/$25 per MTok.
  • Sonnet 5: Default for Pro and Team Standard. It features a native 1M context window with a standard list price of $2/$10 per MTok.
  • Fast Mode: Available for Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 at $10/$50 per MTok.

item.title: Claude CLI and Remote Control receive new features and numerous bug fixes
item.description:
Claude CLI and Remote Control receive new features and numerous bug fixes

Claude’s command‑line interface and Remote Control components received a batch of new settings, commands, and a long list of stability fixes.

🔧 New Features

  • Added an “Organization policy” line to /status andclaude doctor that says why your organization’s policy could not be loaded, such as a proxy not passing the endpoint through.
  • Added bashOutputMaxChars and taskOutputMaxChars settings to raise how much command and background‑task output Claude receives inline before it is saved to a file, up to 128K characters.
  • Added --append-subagent-system-prompt-file to read the subagent system prompt from a file, for prompts too large to pass on the command line.
  • Added /skill-doctor to show which loaded skills go unused and what they cost in context, so you can prune them.

🛠️ Fixes

  • Fixed typed or pasted characters occasionally landing out of order or being dropped during fast input or key repeat.
  • Fixed /add-dir <subdirectory> printing a false “couldn’t be resolved” error when the working directory is on a/net automount.
  • Fixed the Bedrock setup wizard hanging when AWS or an AWS credential helper never responds; it now times out with a clear error, and its model checks now fail correctly behind a TLS‑inspecting proxy.
  • Fixed cloud sessions discarding a plugin synced from claude.ai when managed settings force‑enable it in enabledPlugins, then falling back to a marketplace clone that could fail.
  • Fixed being unable to delete the character immediately before an inline [Image #N] chip in the prompt input.
  • Fixed resuming a session losing hook output and other context around parallel tool calls, which changed the resumed request.
  • Fixed Remote Control showing a stale permission mode when a phone, browser, or claude.ai app attaches to a terminal session or after the mode changes in the terminal.
  • Fixed Remote Control sessions showing as still working (stuck spinner and Stop button) after stopping a turn from a connected phone or browser, or after a local slash command like /clear.
  • Fixed SDK and cloud sessions ignoring a Stop or interrupt sent just after the first prompt, before the turn had started; the turn now stops instead of running to completion.
  • Fixed Remote Control uploading a session pulled with /teleport into the connected session, which appeared appended to the original on phone and web.
  • Fixed Remote Control’s inbound event stream failing behind TLS‑inspecting corporate proxies on native Windows.
  • Fixed Remote Control sessions showing the default effort level on claude.ai when the effort comes from settings.
  • Fixed gcpAuthRefresh opening a browser at startup when the Google credential check was slow, even though the credential was still valid.
  • Fixed claude.ai connectors staying absent for the whole session when the startup connector fetch timed out — the CLI now retries in the background.
  • Fixed sustained high CPU usage when a background agent could not be resumed and its wake‑up was retried in a tight loop.
  • Fixed feature flags gated to a newer version occasionally applying to an older Claude Code version running on the same machine.
  • Fixed /usage and the VS Code usage panel dropping a model‑specific weekly limit row when the usage endpoint is rate limited or when opened right after startup.
  • Fixed claude -p --resume <file> adopting a malformed session ID recorded in the transcript; it now resumes under a fresh session ID instead.
  • Fixed the terminal progress indicator (iTerm2, Ghostty, ConEmu) showing the session as finished while a background workflow or agent was still running.
  • Fixed a rare layout glitch where a box could render with the wrong height after its container switched between row and column direction.
  • Fixed Claude apps gateway client IP when a trusted proxy appends a port to X-Forwarded-For; with an access list set, an unreadable entry now gets 403.
  • Fixed Claude apps gateway telling Claude Desktop to export OpenTelemetry as JSON even when the terminal CLI uses protobuf, so protobuf‑only collectors rejected Desktop’s data.
  • Fixed Desktop and web showing a session as busy while it only watches an artifact for updates.
  • Fixed Claude in Chrome file_upload failing with “paths: expected array, received undefined” in local Cowork sessions run from the Claude Desktop app.
  • Fixed SendMessage to an offline Remote Control session on another machine reading as delivered; the result now says delivery is queued until that machine reconnects.
  • Fixed plugin install hints from CLIs run in background Bash commands: they are now detected, and the raw <claude-code-hint> tag no longer leaks into the conversation.

📊 Impact

These additions expand configurability (organization policy visibility, output size limits, subagent prompts, skill usage diagnostics) while the extensive bug‑fix set improves reliability across CLI, Remote Control, cloud, and integration pathways. Users can now diagnose policy loading issues, capture larger tool outputs inline, manage unused skills, and experience fewer interruptions caused by UI glitches, proxy complications, or session‑management bugs.

#Claude #AItools #BugFixes #CLI #RemoteControl

Source: Releases · anthropics/claude-code
